::: {.pageinfo}
**Builds on** [page 4](violin.qmd): the boundary condition decides which eigenfunctions are allowed. About 7 minutes, plus 4 for the folds.
:::

::: {.puzzle}
**The puzzle.** A clarinet and a flute are about the same length. Yet the clarinet's lowest note is almost an [octave](glossary.qmd#octave) below the flute's. And when the players [overblow](glossary.qmd#overblow), making the tube jump to its next mode (a flutist by blowing faster, a clarinetist by pressing the [register key](glossary.qmd#overblow)), the flute jumps up an octave while the clarinet jumps an [octave and a fifth](glossary.qmd#octave). The same equation governs the air in both tubes. What is different?
:::

Play a fingering on the clarinet, then switch the same tube to a flute, open at both ends, and play it again. Then hold the register key, which makes the tube jump to its next mode, on each; on the flute it stands in for blowing faster.

::: {.family}
**Same operator, other ends.** Stopped organ pipes and pan pipes are closed at one end like the clarinet and share its odd-harmonic spectrum. Open organ pipes share the flute's. Oboes and saxophones have cone-shaped tubes instead of cylinders, a different operator, which this series does not cover.
:::

## Same equation, other ends

**The operator.** Let $p(x, t)$ be the air pressure in the tube minus room pressure. It obeys the wave equation again,
$$
p_{tt} = c^2 p_{xx}, \qquad c^2 = \frac{K}{\rho} \approx (343\ \text{m/s})^2,
$$
where $\rho$ is the density of air and $K$ its [bulk modulus](glossary.qmd#bulk-modulus), its resistance to being squeezed (this $K$ has nothing to do with the bead matrix of page 2). The constant $c$ is the speed of sound, about 343 m/s at 20 °C. So the operator is again $-c^2\,d^2/dx^2$, now acting on pressure shapes along the tube.

::: {.derive}
<details><summary><span class="label">Step-by-step derivation</span>Newton's law for a slab of air <span class="needs">uses partial derivatives</span></summary>

```{=html}
<svg class="fig" viewBox="0 0 420 130" role="img" aria-label="A slab of air in a tube, pushed by pressure on both faces">
  <path class="ink" d="M 20 30 L 400 30 M 20 100 L 400 100"/>
  <rect x="170" y="31" width="80" height="68" class="bar" opacity="0.5"/>
  <path class="pos" d="M 120 65 L 168 65"/><path class="fillpos" d="M 168 59 L 180 65 L 168 71 Z"/>
  <path class="neg" d="M 300 65 L 252 65"/><path class="fillneg" d="M 252 59 L 240 65 L 252 71 Z"/>
  <text x="96" y="58">p(x)</text><text x="300" y="58">p(x+dx)</text>
  <text x="180" y="118">slab, mass ρS dx</text>
</svg>
```

1. Let $\xi(x, t)$ be how far the air that normally sits at $x$ has moved along the tube, and let the tube's cross-section have area $S$.
2. The slab of air between $x$ and $x + dx$ has mass $\rho S\,dx$. The only force on it along the tube is the pressure difference between its two faces, $S\,[p(x) - p(x + dx)] \approx -S\,p_x\,dx$. Newton's law, mass times acceleration equals force, divided by $S\,dx$, is $\rho\,\xi_{tt} = -p_x$.
3. The slab's two faces move by $\xi(x)$ and $\xi(x + dx)$, so its length changes by $\xi(x + dx) - \xi(x) \approx \xi_x\,dx$: it is stretched by the fraction $\xi_x$, and its pressure drops in proportion: $p = -K\,\xi_x$. In a sound wave the squeezing is too fast for heat to flow, which is called [adiabatic](glossary.qmd#bulk-modulus); for air this makes $K$ about 1.4 times atmospheric pressure.
4. Differentiate step 2 in $x$ and step 3 twice in $t$: $\rho\,\xi_{ttx} = -p_{xx}$ and $p_{tt} = -K\,\xi_{xtt}$. Eliminating $\xi$ gives $p_{tt} = (K/\rho)\,p_{xx}$.

What was assumed: the tube is narrow compared with the sound's wavelength, so the pressure is the same across it, and the pressure changes are small. Friction with the walls is left out.

</details>
:::

**Boundary conditions.** At an open end the air in the tube meets the room, so the pressure there is room pressure: $p = 0$. This is approximate: the air just outside moves with the air inside, so the tube acts as if it were slightly longer, by about 0.6 of its radius at each open end, an amount called the *end correction*. At the clarinet's reed the opening is nearly shut, so the air there cannot move back and forth. Air that never moves has no acceleration, so the net push on it is zero; that push is set by how fast the pressure changes along the tube, $p_x$, so $p_x = 0$ there (step 2 of the derivation, with $\xi$ the air's displacement along the tube). The first of these is the string's Dirichlet condition. The second, a condition on the slope, is called a *Neumann condition*.

**Spectrum.** A mode is a pressure shape $X(x)$ with $-X'' = k^2 X$, so $X = a\cos kx + b\sin kx$, and its frequency is $f = ck/2\pi$. For the clarinet, $X'(0) = bk = 0$ at the reed forces $b = 0$, leaving $X = \cos kx$, and $X(L) = 0$ at the open end needs $\cos kL = 0$, so $kL = (2n - 1)\pi/2$ and $f_n = (2n-1)c/4L$. For the flute, open at both ends, the conditions are the string's, and give $\sin(n\pi x/L)$. So

| | ends | eigenfunctions | frequencies |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| flute | open, open | $\sin(n\pi x/L)$ | $f_n = n\,\dfrac{c}{2L}$ |
| clarinet | closed, open | $\cos\big((2n-1)\pi x/2L\big)$ | $f_n = (2n-1)\,\dfrac{c}{4L}$ |

Two consequences can be heard in the demo.

- **An octave lower, almost.** An octave is a frequency ratio of 2. The same ideal tube sounds $c/4L$ closed at one end but $c/2L$ open at both, exactly an octave lower. Real flutes and clarinets differ a little in length, the clarinet's mouthpiece and bell change its effective length, and the end corrections differ, so the real interval comes out a bit less than an octave.
- **A twelfth, not an octave.** The clarinet's register key opens a small hole near the top of the tube. An open hole lets air in and out, pulling the pressure there toward room pressure, which spoils the fundamental, a mode that needs pressure variation at that point. For one note in the lower part of the low register (the notes played without the key), the hole sits about a third of the way down the sounding tube, right where that note's $3f_1$ mode has no pressure variation anyway, so the open hole does not disturb that mode (Wolfe). For the other notes the hole is off that point, well off for the lowest and highest notes you play with the key (Wolfe), and a second effect helps: the air in a small hole has mass, and the faster it must move back and forth, the harder it is to move. At the fundamental's lower frequency it moves more easily, so the hole leaks enough to spoil that mode; at the higher frequency of the $3f_1$ mode it moves much less, so the hole acts almost as a plug. Either way the tube jumps to the $3f_1$ mode. That is a ratio of 3, called a twelfth: an octave and a fifth, where a fifth is the ratio 3/2. A flutist overblows without a key, by blowing faster, and the flute's next mode is $2f_1$, an octave. That is why clarinet fingerings repeat a twelfth apart and flute fingerings an octave apart.

::: {.derive}
<details><summary><span class="label">Proof</span>Why only odd harmonics: the closed tube is a quarter of a loop <span class="needs">uses the circle's eigenfunctions (page 3)</span></summary>

Use the reflections from the [string page](violin.qmd). Take a pressure shape $p$ on $[0, L]$ with $p_x(0) = 0$ and $p(L) = 0$.

1. Reflect it *evenly* across the reed end, $p(-x) = p(x)$. A smooth even shape has zero slope at 0, so even reflection is what the Neumann condition $p_x(0) = 0$ allows, so the result is a shape on $[-L, L]$ that vanishes at both ends.
2. Reflect that *oddly* across $x = L$, $p(2L - x) = -p(x)$, and repeat. The result is a shape on a loop of circumference $4L$.
3. On that loop the eigenfunctions are $\cos(k\pi x/2L)$ and $\sin(k\pi x/2L)$. Step 1 keeps only cosines. Step 2 needs $\cos\big(k\pi(2L - x)/2L\big) = (-1)^k\cos(k\pi x/2L)$ to equal $-\cos(k\pi x/2L)$, which keeps only odd $k$.

So the clarinet's modes are the odd harmonics of a loop four tube-lengths long, which is where both the factor 4 and the odd numbers come from.

</details>
:::

**The reed.** The reed is a valve. When the pressure in the mouthpiece drops, it closes, and when the pressure rises, it opens, so the air column, through the pressure it creates, drives the reed that feeds it. In normal playing this settles into a [periodic](glossary.qmd#periodic) oscillation, like the bowed string, at a playing frequency close to the tube's lowest mode. A periodic sound can have partials only at whole-number multiples of the playing frequency, but it may have them at all of them, so the distinction matters: the tube's *modes* are odd multiples only, but the clarinet's *sound* contains even harmonics too. In the low register, the lowest notes of the instrument, the even harmonics are weak because the tube has no resonance to support them, but they are not absent. A real clarinet's bore is not exactly cylindrical, and its holes and bell matter; they refine these numbers, not the picture.

## What we found

The string's operator also governs the air pressure in a tube. Changing the boundary condition at one end, from "pressure equals the room's" to "the air cannot move", halves the lowest frequency and keeps only its odd multiples: the clarinet's modes are at 1, 3, 5, … times $c/4L$. In the sound, which repeats, the even harmonics are weak rather than gone.

## The next puzzle

So far every restoring force has been a pull or a push along the material: tension along a string, pressure along a tube. A kalimba tine is different, because nothing stretches it. Halve a string's length and its pitch rises one octave; halve a tine's length and its pitch rises two. Why?

[← A string with ends](violin.qmd) · [Next: change the order →](kalimba.qmd)

N. H. Fletcher and T. D. Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments*, 2nd ed., Springer, 1998: chapter 8 (pipes) and chapter 15 (woodwind reed instruments).
:::

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, CSOUND = 343, LTOT = 0.585;
  var SEMIS = [11, 9, 7, 5, 4, 2]; // holes from the reed toward the bell
  var HOLES = SEMIS.map(function (s) { return LTOT * Math.pow(2, -s / 12); });
  var open = [false, false, false, false, false, false], reg = false, flute = false, voice = null;
  var FING = [{ n: "1", s: 0 }, { n: "2", s: 2 }, { n: "3", s: 4 }, { n: "4", s: 5 }, { n: "5", s: 7 }, { n: "6", s: 9 }, { n: "7", s: 11 }];
  function setFingering(s) { for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++) open[i] = s > 0 && SEMIS[i] <= s; update(); }
  function Leff() { for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++) if (open[i]) return HOLES[i]; return LTOT; }
  function modeN() { return reg ? 2 : 1; }
  function freq() { var L = Leff(); return flute ? modeN() * CSOUND / (2 * L) : (2 * modeN() - 1) * CSOUND / (4 * L); }
  function parts() { return C.models.clarinet.partials({ flute: flute }); }

  var fing = document.getElementById("fing");
  FING.forEach(function (fg) { var b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.textContent = fg.n; b.setAttribute("aria-label", "Fingering " + fg.n); b.addEventListener("click", function () { setFingering(fg.s); }); fing.appendChild(b); });

  function startBlow() {
    if (voice) return; var a = C.ac(), t = a.currentTime, osc = a.createOscillator(), g = a.createGain(), lp = a.createBiquadFilter();
    osc.setPeriodicWave(C.wave(a, parts())); osc.frequency.value = freq();
    lp.type = "lowpass"; lp.frequency.value = flute ? 3500 : 4500;
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0, t); g.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(flute ? 0.4 : 0.3, t + 0.06);
    osc.connect(lp); lp.connect(g); g.connect(C.out); osc.start();
    voice = { osc: osc, g: g, lp: lp }; document.getElementById("blow").classList.add("on");
  }
  function stopBlow() {
    if (!voice) return; var t = C.ac().currentTime; voice.g.gain.cancelScheduledValues(t); voice.g.gain.setTargetAtTime(0, t, 0.04); voice.osc.stop(t + 0.4); voice = null;
    document.getElementById("blow").classList.remove("on");
  }
  function update() {
    if (voice) { var a = C.ac(); voice.osc.frequency.setTargetAtTime(freq(), a.currentTime, 0.01); voice.osc.setPeriodicWave(C.wave(a, parts())); voice.lp.frequency.value = flute ? 3500 : 4500; }
    var f = freq(), nn = C.noteName(f), L = Leff();
    document.getElementById("cRead").innerHTML = "sounding length <b>" + (L * 100).toFixed(1) + " cm</b> · mode " + (flute ? modeN() + " → " + modeN() + "c/2L" : modeN() + " → " + (2 * modeN() - 1) + "c/4L") + " · <b>" + f.toFixed(1) + " Hz</b> · " + nn.name + (nn.cents ? (nn.cents > 0 ? " +" : " ") + nn.cents + "¢" : "");
    C.stems(document.getElementById("cSpec"), parts().slice(0, 12), { W: 320, H: 90, rmax: 12, fs: 8, sw: 2.5 });
  }
  var blow = document.getElementById("blow");
  blow.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); blow.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); startBlow(); });
  blow.addEventListener("pointerup", stopBlow); blow.addEventListener("pointercancel", stopBlow);
  // capture phase, so the page claims its keys before the blog's search shortcut sees them
  function mine(e) { var k = parseInt(e.key, 10); return e.code === "Space" || (k >= 1 && k <= 7); }
  window.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
    if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || (e.target && e.target.tagName === "INPUT") || !mine(e)) return;
    e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); if (e.repeat) return;
    if (e.code === "Space") { startBlow(); return; }
    setFingering(FING[parseInt(e.key, 10) - 1].s);
  }, true);
  window.addEventListener("keyup", function (e) {
    if (!mine(e)) return; e.stopPropagation();
    if (e.code === "Space") stopBlow();
  }, true);
  var regB = document.getElementById("reg");
  regB.addEventListener("click", function () { reg = !reg; regB.setAttribute("aria-pressed", reg); update(); });
  function setType(fl) { flute = fl; document.getElementById("tClar").setAttribute("aria-pressed", !fl); document.getElementById("tFlute").setAttribute("aria-pressed", fl); update(); }
  document.getElementById("tClar").addEventListener("click", function () { setType(false); });
  document.getElementById("tFlute").addEventListener("click", function () { setType(true); });

  var cv = document.getElementById("pipe"), ctx = cv.getContext("2d");
  function geom() { var d = C.fit(cv), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, x0 = 30 * d, x1 = W - 16 * d; return { d: d, W: W, H: H, x0: x0, x1: x1, top: H * 0.32, bot: H * 0.68 }; }
  function X(g, L) { return g.x0 + (g.x1 - g.x0) * L / LTOT; }
  cv.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) {
    var r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(), g = geom(), px = (e.clientX - r.left) * g.d, best = -1, bd = 26 * g.d;
    HOLES.forEach(function (L, i) { var dx = Math.abs(X(g, L) - px); if (dx < bd) { bd = dx; best = i; } });
    if (best >= 0) { open[best] = !open[best]; update(); }
  });
  function draw(now) {
    var g = geom(), d = g.d, L = Leff(), xe = X(g, L), n = modeN();
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, g.W, g.H);
    var ph = C.reduce || !voice ? 1 : Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * 0.8 * now / 1000);
    for (var px = Math.floor(g.x0); px < g.x1; px += Math.max(1, Math.round(d))) {
      var xx = (px - g.x0) / (g.x1 - g.x0) * LTOT, amp;
      if (xx <= L) {
        var u = xx / L;
        amp = flute ? Math.sin(n * Math.PI * u) : Math.cos((2 * n - 1) * Math.PI * u / 2);
        var v = amp * ph, c = v >= 0 ? C.col["--pos"] : C.col["--neg"];
        ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb(c, Math.min(1, Math.abs(v)) * 0.85 + 0.05);
      } else ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--grid", 0.5);
      ctx.fillRect(px, g.top, Math.max(1, Math.round(d)), g.bot - g.top);
    }
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.lineWidth = 2 * d; ctx.strokeRect(g.x0, g.top, g.x1 - g.x0, g.bot - g.top);
    if (flute) { ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--paper"); ctx.fillRect(g.x0 - 2 * d, g.top + 2 * d, 4 * d, g.bot - g.top - 4 * d); }
    else { ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(g.x0, g.top); ctx.lineTo(g.x0 - 22 * d, (g.top + g.bot) / 2 - 3 * d); ctx.lineTo(g.x0 - 22 * d, (g.top + g.bot) / 2 + 3 * d); ctx.lineTo(g.x0, g.bot); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill(); }
    HOLES.forEach(function (Lh, i) {
      var x = X(g, Lh), r = 9 * d;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, g.top - r - 6 * d, r, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
      if (open[i]) { ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--paper"); ctx.fill(); ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.lineWidth = 2 * d; ctx.stroke(); }
      else { ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.fill(); }
      ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--muted"); ctx.fillRect(x - 1 * d, g.top - 6 * d, 2 * d, 6 * d);
    });
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--accent"); ctx.lineWidth = 2 * d; ctx.setLineDash([4 * d, 4 * d]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(xe, g.top - 2 * d); ctx.lineTo(xe, g.bot + 14 * d); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--muted"); ctx.font = (11 * d) + "px 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace"; ctx.textAlign = "center";
    ctx.fillText("effective end", xe, g.bot + 26 * d);
    ctx.textAlign = "left"; ctx.fillText(flute ? "open" : "reed", 4 * d, g.bot + 26 * d);
    requestAnimationFrame(draw);
  }
  C.onTheme(update);
  update(); requestAnimationFrame(draw);
})();
</script>
```
